exposure: Antenatal care attendance (four or more visits)
cohort: The study included 552 mothers from Tema General Hospital in Ghana, comparing those who experienced stillbirths to those who had live births in 2019.
finding: The study identified advanced maternal age (40+), maternal employment, caesarean section, low birth weight, and maternal hypertension as factors significantly increasing the likelihood of stillbirth, while higher maternal education and adequate antenatal care significantly lowered it.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was found to significantly increase the likelihood of stillbirth (aOR = 1.9).
birth_weight: Infants with low birth weight were included as a variable associated with increased likelihood of stillbirth.
